title: A write through a wider shape view stores an object of the wrong class in an anonymous object, and a narrower view's typed read reads the wrong object's memory.
text: `rule:types/shape-type` compares a shape's field types by ordinary assignability, and a shape value is aliased rather than copied. So with `type Narrow = {pet: Dog}; type Wide = {pet: Animal};`, the program `Narrow $n = {pet: new Dog()}; Wide $w = $n; $w->pet = new Animal(); echo $n->pet->legs;` prints a garbage integer. An anonymous object's class is named for its field names alone (`nvs_ir::lower::shape_class_label`), so its slot carries a tag and nothing else, and `Tag::Object` answers for every class. The same holds for an array's elements and a union's arms in such a slot, and for an erased write into one. A declared class's slot is checked in full (`ClassDesc::field_checks`). Closing it is a decision for the user: make a shape's mutable fields invariant in the checker, carry a declared type per anonymous object at run time, or refuse a write through a view wider than the value's own.
